free_tier.stated: No free tier and no trial: block accounts only, 5 GB for USD 1.99 up to 3,072 GB for USD 99.99.
free_tier.notes: the block is the product; there is no monthly plan on the page

per_object_cap.stated: Not applicable: usenet articles are capped by the poster's segment size, not by the provider.

retention.stated: The block never expires: 'No Expiration! Keep Your Gigs Until Used!' and 'Pay Only ONCE! Never Any Rebilling!' Article retention is described only as 'leading retention, increasing day by day' with no number on the page.
retention.notes: null is indefinite for the prepaid bytes; the article retention has no published figure, so the two clocks must not be confused

egress.terms: Downloaded bytes are drawn from the purchased block; there is no monthly allowance to renew and no rebilling.
egress.price_per_tb: USD 39.99 per TB in the 1,024 GB block

tooling: any NNTP client or downloader (SABnzbd, NZBGet, nzbget-compatible tooling); no API beyond NNTP
chaining: the cleanest 'fetch now, read later' primitive in the whole corpus: a prepaid byte balance that survives any pause, and articles that sit on the provider's spool independent of a user's payment state

limits.value: the purchased block, 5 GB to 3,072 GB
blocks from 5 GB to 3,072 GB, one-time and non-expiring

limits_note: Article retention is the real ceiling and it is unpublished, which is the one gap in an otherwise clean offer.
binding_note: At 1 TiB/month the block is spent in about a month; that is the point - it is spent, not expired, and an unspent balance waits indefinitely.

identity_cost.detail: email and password at the billing portal; no identity document

reliability_note: Completeness depends on the poster's propagation; the FAQ page answered a bot challenge to the reader, so no completeness figure could be read.
confidence_note: The non-expiring claim is on the vendor's own front page in two places. Article retention has no number there and the FAQ was challenge-walled, so one figure is missing rather than guessed.

evidence.proved: 'No Expiration! Keep Your Gigs Until Used!', 'Pay Only ONCE! Never Any Rebilling!', the 5 GB to 3,072 GB price ladder, 200 connections, seven server locations
the FAQ returned a 403 bot challenge to every reader route tried (extractor, exa, contextdev, hyperbrowser, tinyfish, cfbr), so its retention figure is unread
5 GB $1.99 through 3,072 GB $99.99; 'Pay Only ONCE! Never Any Rebilling!'; 'No Expiration!'; 'up to 200 connections'; seven server locations
BlockNews on NetNews, AS6450; reseller of the same backbone as Frugal Usenet

notes: What it does not give is storage of a file a user chose - it gives access to articles the provider happens to hold. At $32.55/TB it is cheaper than every UsenetExpress block except CubeNet's 2 TB tier, and it sits on a different backbone, which is what a fill account needs.

extras.reactivation: nothing to reactivate: the balance is the account

interface_detail: NNTP with SSL; up to 200 connections; seven server locations (two USA, one Europe, plus Africa, Asia, Australia, South America)
